title: Ordered and unordered lists
learningObjectives: Choose and use semantic list elements correctly

understand.concept: Use ul for a group where order does not change meaning and ol when sequence or ranking matters. Each item belongs in li.
understand.whyItMatters: Correct list semantics expose relationships and sequence to assistive technologies.
understand.analogy: Think of a shopping list or a glossary.
understand.analogyLimit: Not every visually indented block is a semantic list; HTML structure determines meaning.

explain.narrative: Use ul for a group where order does not change meaning and ol when sequence or ranking matters. Each item belongs in li.

examples.explanation: Check that each child item is inside the correct parent list element.
examples.expectedOutput: The browser renders a semantic list.

practise.guidedTask: Change the items in the example and inspect the list structure.
practise.independentTask: Build a course outline or navigation menu using semantic lists.
hints: Use ol only when order matters.
Keep nested lists inside the relevant list item.
